scorecards.inningsCommentary: Bangladesh commenced their first innings at Shere Bangla National Stadium, aiming to set an imposing baseline total. The centerpiece of the innings was a brilliant 136 from Mohammad Mahmudullah, complemented by a commanding 111-run stand between Mohammad Mahmudullah and Shakib Hasan that absorbed bowling hostility and accelerated the scoring rate to 3.28 RPO. KC Brathwaite (2/57) maintained tight lines for West Indies, creating intermittent chances in an otherwise demanding fielding effort. Finishing at 508/10 (153.6 ov), Bangladesh established an overwhelming first-innings foundation that firmly dictated the terms of the match.

summaryTab.matchCommentary:
The Test match at Shere Bangla National Stadium commenced with high tactical intensity as Bangladesh posted 508/10 (153.6 ov) in their opening innings. In response, West Indies countered with 111/10 (36.4 ov), setting the stage for a compelling contest of tactical endurance. Early sessions tested batting resolve against disciplined seam movement, with both attacks striving to gain the upper hand on a developing surface.

The defining turning point arrived during 7-Wicket Spell: Mehidy Miraz (7/58), which irrevocably altered the trajectory of the match. As the match progressed through its pivotal middle stages, Mehidy Miraz delivered a masterclass for Bangladesh (18 Runs & 12 Wkts), absorbing intense pressure and tilting the momentum decisively. Crucial partnership stands and incisive bowling spells broke the opposition's resistance, shifting the control share (Bangladesh 54%) and allowing Bangladesh to dictate terms heading into the decisive sessions.

Entering the final innings, West Indies faced an uphill battle under unrelenting scoreboard pressure. Bangladesh's bowling unit, bolstered by Shakib Hasan (80 Runs & 4 Wkts), maintained relentless discipline and attacked the stumps relentlessly. Wicket clusters in the closing sessions dismantled any remaining resistance, sealing Bangladesh won by innings & 184 runs in comprehensive fashion.

Verdict: Bangladesh's triumph was built on superior pressure absorption, clinical execution during critical moments, and the ability to dominate key sessions. While West Indies produced fighting phases, Bangladesh won the pivotal turning points and sustained higher tactical control across all five days to emerge as deserved victors.
